posts.name: McBehrer
posts.cooked:
I disagree. Jack Handle is definitely the problem. The fact that it takes a single instance of damage and splits it up into multiple instances of damage (which are actually just multiple, SINGLE INSTANCES of damage) without regard for who the initial target was means that it has plenty of room for exploitation. Without such a poorly-worded card, Friendly Fire has no design flaws. I get the way Jack Handle SHOULD work -- a weak punch becomes a broad, sweeping attack that hits multiple targets -- but the way it is now and the way it interacts with cards like Infection and FF make no sense from a thematic OR mechanical standpoint. Infection: you have an infection. Holding a stick can make you magically turn the infection outward and hit things with it. WAT. Friendly fire: Setback gets in the way and gets hit. Holding a stick makes Setback reflect the hit infinitely until literally everything is dead. WAT.

 

Jack Handle needs to change. Friendly Fire does not. There are several ways to change it without changing the intent.

 

"Whenever Mr. Fixer would deal damage to a target -- either by using a power or playing a card -- prevent that damage and instead Mr. Fixer deals that damage to all non-hero targets."

"Whenever Mr. Fixer would deal damage to a non-hero target, deal that damage to each non-hero target instead. Damage dealt this way is not affected by this card's effect."

"The first time Mr. Fixer would deal damage each phase, instead deal that damage to each non-hero target."
